name: Question 1
worked_solution:
First, we substitute $u={x}^{3}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u={x}^{2}\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to -\infty $ when $x\to -\infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u={x}^{3}$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $0$ | $-\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $-\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{x}^{2}\cdot {5}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{5}^{u}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Now, we proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{x}^{2}\cdot {5}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}{5}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{{5}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}]}_{a}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }[{5}^{u}]_{a}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }(1-{5}^{a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(1-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{5}^{a})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, recall the end behavior of the function $y={5}^{a},$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{a\to -\infty }{5}^{a}=0$

- ${lim}_{a\to \infty }{5}^{a}=\infty $

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14070214/assets/c0c7699b036ebd8779cd6c3d3143cdcca6312834ee731e144e38488124164f43.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}{x}^{2}\cdot {5}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(1-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{5}^{a}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the integral in terms of the new variable u is

∫−∞0x2⋅5x3dx=13∫−∞05udu.

Now, we proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter a, integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as a→−∞.

∫−∞0x2⋅5x3dx=13lima→−∞∫a05udu=13lima→−∞[5uln⁡5]a0=13ln⁡5lima→−∞[5u]a0=13ln⁡5lima→−∞(1−5a)=13ln⁡5(1−lima→−∞5a)

Next, recall the end behavior of the function y=5a, shown in the graph below:

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

∫−∞0x2⋅5x3dx=13ln⁡5(1−lima→−∞5a)=13ln⁡5(1−0)=13ln⁡5.
